report.headline: Projected usage climbs from 16.1% to 22.2% in the EuroLeague, but the shooting efficiency projection carries no signal and the interval on usage alone spans nearly two league standard deviations.

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to rise from 16.1% in the NBA to 22.2% in the EuroLeague, above the league's minutes-weighted average of 20.4% (sd 4.2%), and the model beats the trivial league-average baseline on this metric (3.3% error vs 4.3%).

risks.text: The true shooting projection (56.3%) is not usable: the model's error on this metric (4.7% MAE over 367 transitions) is identical to that of the naive league-average baseline (4.7%), so it is described in the evidence as not to be trusted.

Even the trustworthy usage projection carries a wide band: the 80% interval (18.0%-26.4%) covers about two standard deviations of the EuroLeague usage distribution (sd 4.2%), meaning individual placement within that range is uncertain even though the group-level shift upward is credible.

He entered the source season already well below the NBA average in usage (-0.82 sd) and slightly below average in true shooting (-0.20 sd), and the broader cohort of 115 NBA-to-EuroLeague movers this estimate rests on sat, on average, 0.31 sd below their own league's average at the time of the move — an atypical group to project from.

strengths.text: In the source NBA season he produced 12.628 points and 4.677 rebounds per 75 possessions on 53.0% true shooting, with 49.0% of his shot attempts coming from three.
A 12.2% turnover rate accompanies a projected jump in possession share, from 16.1% usage in the NBA to a projected 22.2% in the EuroLeague.

The usage projection is one the model has actually validated: on 367 held-out transitions its usage-rate error (3.3%) beats the best trivial baseline (4.3%), and the fitted slope of 0.986 indicates his standing relative to his league is expected to carry across almost fully.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate runs from 18.0% to 26.4% and the 95% interval from 15.8% to 28.6%, a spread of roughly two EuroLeague usage-rate standard deviations (sd 4.2%), so the model can rank this player against peers but not fix a precise number. The true shooting projection of 56.3% should not be trusted at all: its out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the league average (also 4.7%).
